soak.why_a_timer_cannot_express_this: MI-49's bar for the operator's conditional widening is explicit that time and quiet DO NOT COUNT: 'at least one bybit_coverage_soak row on bybit_1 carries verdicts_differ: true -- i.e. the graded and side-blind bases actually reached OPPOSITE verdicts, so arming demonstrably changed an outcome'. check_every_days says how often a session must LOOK; this says what it is looking FOR. ⚠️ AND THE THIRD STATE IS THE ONE THIS BLOCK EXISTS FOR: once the gate is armed, an empty log stops meaning 'not yet' and starts meaning the writer is DEAD -- which a timer can never distinguish from patience, and which would otherwise leave the operator waiting indefinitely on evidence that was never coming.
soak.not_writing_is_EXPECTED_until_the_arm_is: ⚠️ DO NOT ACT ON A not_writing VERDICT BEFORE THE ARM IS CONFIRMED. Arming is HELD by operator sequencing (MI-49), and at BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_MODE=off the writer returns before writing by design, so zero rows is the CORRECT state today and says nothing about the writer's health. The verdict only becomes a finding after BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_MODE=apply and BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_ACCOUNTS=bybit_1 are read back off /proc/<MainPID>/environ -- never off the .env, which says only what the NEXT restart will pick up. Until then this row grades `unknown` (no probe is declared), which is the honest answer.

items.detail: MITIGATED, NOT FIXED, in the evidence-floor-horizon PR: the generator now publishes n_decisions, n_filled, execution, window_days and the evidence_horizon block ON THE INDEX, so the diagnosis no longer NEEDS the join — which removes the reason a reader would cross the boundary, without removing the boundary. scripts/ml/evidence_floor_report.py stamps sources_agree per row for anyone who still joins. items.detail: /api/bot/trades/closed and /api/bot/performance now carry journalTrust, resolved from comms/broker_truth_ledger.json. That ledger lists bybit_2 and nothing else, because it is populated BY HAND from an operator's venue export. So every other account grades `no_record`, which means NOBODY HAS RECONCILED IT — never that it reconciles. A session reading `no_record` as a clean bill of health has reintroduced the exact bug the field was built to fix.

items.the_confound_that_makes_it_hard: It is a COUNTERFACTUAL problem: we observe the winner's outcome and never the loser's, so a live correlation between `decided_by` and realised R is confounded by which strategies tend to win under each tier. CARRIED FORWARD from OI-20260827-RESEARCH-QUEUE-DISPATCHER-NEVER-FIRED, which was CLEARED on 2026-08-31. That row's two criteria were met and are recorded below; this row exists so the one caveat inside it does not vanish with it — clearing a row must not delete the knowledge it held.

WHAT CLEARED, with evidence read rather than inferred:
(a) A SCHEDULED dispatcher run dispatched a real job and its rows landed in the store the job declares. Run 33340458710 (event=schedule, 2026-08-30T22:56:22Z) logged `RQ-20260827-001 dispatched gld-compat-matrix.yml on main (route=runner)`, and docs/research/gld-compat-matrix-verdicts.jsonl on main carries 11 rows at run_generated_at=2026-08-30T22:56:50Z — 28 seconds later. Verified by READING the store, not by a workflow exit code. The next scheduled run repeats it at 23:34:31Z.
(b) The cadence stamp race was exercised. RQ-20260830-002 (cadence: monthly) fired at 12:29:28Z; on the NEXT dispatcher run the same job logged `not_due — last ran 2026-08-30T12:29:28+00:00, cadence monthly not yet elapsed`.

⚠️ THE CLEARED ROW ALSO SAID 'its cron has never fired', AND THAT WAS STALE — 5 of 8 dispatcher runs carry event=schedule. It understated progress while, separately, hiding a real regression: the two most recent SCHEDULED runs both FAILED, on BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH (the dispatch itself succeeded; the stamp PR never merged). That failure is tracked on the backlog row, not here.

WHAT IS UNPROVEN AND IS THIS ROW'S SUBJECT: the queue has never held a GPU-routed job, so the ledger preflight has never been observed either refusing or admitting a run. Nothing about the runner route is evidence about the GPU route — different branch, different gate, real money.
items.clears_when: A GPU-routed job is fired once and the ledger preflight is OBSERVED making a decision — either refusing the run on budget or admitting it — read from that run's own output, not from a test or a dry run. Both outcomes clear it; what does not clear it is a GPU job that never reached the preflight, or a runner-routed job however many times it succeeds.

probe.checks: Looks for a gpu-burst-train.yml run whose logs carry the preflight step at all, over the last 20 runs. ⚠️ THE REASON THIS ROW CARRIED FOR HAVING NO PROBE WAS A CATEGORY ERROR, which is why it now has one: it said a scheduled probe 'cannot produce that without FIRING a GPU job, which spends real budget'. True about FIRING and irrelevant to PROBING — NO probe in this family produces the event it watches (pairs_soak does not open a pair; arbitration_fanout_soak does not route an order). Conflating producing an observation with observing it turned a buildable probe into a declared impossibility. This fires no job, spends nothing, and only reads.
probe.is_not: ⚠️ A PASS HERE IS THE WEAKEST IN THE FAMILY AND MUST NOT CLEAR THE ROW ON ITS OWN. clears_when demands the preflight be OBSERVED MAKING A DECISION — refusing on budget or admitting — and explicitly rules out a dry run. This cannot separate those: with GPU_BURST_ARMED != 1 the workflow runs a DRY PREFLIGHT ONLY, and its log carries the same step name as an armed run. So a pass means 'a run exists that reached the preflight step', and a session must read that run's own output to see whether it was armed and what it decided. The literal is deliberately the step name rather than a decision string, because no decision string has ever been observed in a real run — inventing one would be a predicate matching nothing while looking precise. Tighten it to the real decision line the first time an armed run happens. Since the event never occurs spontaneously, a FAIL here means 'nobody has fired one', not 'the gate is broken'.

items.summary: session-brief-guard is diff-scoped now, so a brief that goes stale on the CLOCK can no longer fail a PR that did not touch the registers. The `inherited` verdict has NEVER been emitted by a real CI run — it is deployed, not proven.
items.observation:
WHY THIS EXISTS. `render_session_brief` calls `datetime.now()` and `due_items` flips a monitoring row to DUE once `check_every_days` elapses, so the block COMMITTED in CLAUDE.md goes stale at a UTC-midnight boundary with no commit anywhere. The whole-tree `--check` then reds EVERY open PR until a human re-renders, and nothing re-runs a branch's checks, so a branch cut inside that window is stranded permanently.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, not inferred: OI-20260826-MHG-OVER-COVER-MECHANISM-UNVERIFIED (verified_at 2026-08-29, check_every_days 2) crossed into DUE at 00:00Z. PRs #10538 (00:47Z) and #10539 (01:22Z) BOTH failed on exactly `session-brief-guard` — read from the job logs, not guessed — with pytest-run, pytest-collect and repo-inventory GREEN on both. CLAUDE.md was not re-rendered until 06:47Z. Merging current main into each branch (operator-approved) turned `guards` GREEN on both with no content change, which is the positive control that the cause was the clock and not their rows.

STATE THE POPULATION: 2 of the 3 stranded automation PRs were inspected. #10398 was NOT examined (operator said do not touch it), so it is NOT claimed to share this cause.

WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN: every test of the fix is synthetic — a temp git repo built by tests/test_session_brief_diff_scope.py. No REAL CI run has printed `verdict=inherited`, which is the only evidence the diff-scoped path behaves on a live PR (a `--base origin/main` that cannot resolve in the guards job would grade `base_unreadable` and FAIL CLOSED — the same red as before, for a different reason, which is exactly the confusion this row exists to catch). The one-shot `commit-to-main` refresh is likewise unexercised: no run has reported a `stale-branch refresh -> ...` notice.

=== 2026-08-31, HALF (a) STILL OPEN; THE FINDING CLAUSE IS RULED OUT. ===
The diff-scoped guard ran in real CI twice on PR #10575 (`guards` green on both 00cfb57e and
d4f4c745, with `--check --base origin/main`). It printed `clean`, NOT `inherited` — the brief
was current on both sides, so half (a) is genuinely unmet rather than quietly satisfied.
⚠️ But the FINDING this row names — `verdict=base_unreadable`, i.e. origin/main not resolving
in the guards job — DID NOT OCCUR. That was the specific risk of shipping a ref-dependent
check, and it is now ruled out by observation rather than by reasoning.
Half (b) also unmet, correctly: the dispatcher's stamp PR (#10576) merged without stalling,
so the one-shot refresh had nothing to do and printed no `stale-branch refresh ->` line.
Neither half can be forced; both need a PR that opens across a cadence boundary.
items.clears_when: BOTH: (a) a real CI run prints `session-brief: verdict=inherited` on a PR that did not touch the registers, found in that run's job log rather than reasoned about; and (b) a `commit-to-main` run prints `stale-branch refresh -> refreshed` or `-> not_needed_up_to_date`, proving the branch is on the new code path at all. A passing synthetic test is NEITHER half. If instead a run prints `verdict=base_unreadable`, that is a FINDING — `origin/main` is not resolvable in the guards job — and the fix is the ref, not this row.

probe.checks: BOTH halves, in the two DIFFERENT workflows that print them, because clears_when requires both and a pass on one half is the over-read this family exists to prevent. (a) `session-brief: verdict=inherited` in a guards.yml run — emitted only by render_session_brief.py's inherited branch, so its presence IS the diff-scoping path having been taken on a real PR. (b) `commit-to-main: stale-branch refresh ->` in a due-list.yml run — the composite action prints it with the resulting state, proving the automation branch is on the new code path at all. Each group is scanned over the last 20 runs and EVERY group must hit. The positive control `session-brief:` appears in essentially every guards run, so a workflow rename, an expired log or a revoked token becomes could_not_look instead of a permanent quiet negative.
probe.is_not: A pass does NOT establish that half (a) came from a PR that genuinely did not touch the registers — the log line does not carry the diff, and `inherited` is explicitly NOT 'the brief is fine', it is 'this PR did not break it'. Nor does it tell which of `-> refreshed` and `-> not_needed_up_to_date` half (b) printed; clears_when accepts either, but they mean different things and a session grading the mechanism should read which. ⚠️ THIS READER HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST THE REAL ACTIONS API: api.github.com is intercepted at HTTP 403 from a Claude Code on the web sandbox, so its controls run against a fake server and its FIRST scheduled run is its real verification. That is safe only because a broken reader here reports could_not_run, never fail — if this row shows could_not_run after the probes workflow has run, suspect the reader before the mechanism. Finally, clears_when's own escape hatch stands: a run printing `verdict=base_unreadable` is a FINDING about the ref, not evidence for this row, and no probe makes that call.

items.summary: scope-overlap-audit works — its FIRST GENUINE catch landed 2026-08-31T17:26Z. But the same comment ALSO reported this session's own board START back at it, because the attributor compares the START's branch to the PR's branch and a session posts ONE START while opening PRs from SEVERAL branches. Read an overlap comment expecting one line of it to be yours.
items.clears_when: A scope-overlap comment on a PR from a session that posted its START under a DIFFERENT branch name lists that START under the `mine` attribution (i.e. it is NOT rendered as another session's) — read from the comment body. The proposed fix is a session-suffix match; any fix that achieves the above clears this.
items.observation: MEASURED 2026-08-31T17:26:46Z on PR #10607, read from the posted comment, not from the code. It reported `Compared 3 changed file(s) against 66 declared path(s) — 6 attributed to another session, 2 unattributable`. THE GENUINE HALF IS REAL AND IS THE FIRST ONE: `claude/research-queue-landing-v4yfq7` (11:41Z, 15:24Z) and `claude/research-disposition-resweep-cplgnv` (15:55Z) had both declared `docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json`, and the latter also `ROADMAP.md` and `docs/sprint-logs/` — all three files this PR changes. That supersedes any claim that the detector has never caught a real overlap; it has. THE DEFECT IS THE THIRD LINE: `claude/workflows-audit-restructure-fz0sw9` is THIS session's own designated branch, and the PR was opened from `claude/session-wrapup-fz0sw9`, so `attribution()`'s `branch == my_branch` test graded the session's own START as `other`. This is the SAME false-positive class fixed in #10594, in a narrower form — that fix handled a START with no branch; this is a START with a DIFFERENT branch from the same session. It is the COMMON shape, not an edge case: a session posts one START and opens per-task branches. PROPOSED FIX (small, not applied here): the trailing 6-char session suffix is shared across a session's branches (`fz0sw9`, `v4yfq7`, `cplgnv`), so match on that suffix in addition to the exact branch. It must ADD to `mine`, never suppress an `other` — under-reporting a real overlap is the worse error, which is why the `unattributable` state already resolves toward reporting. ⚠️ NOT A BLOCKER FOR #10607: the overlap was verified harmless — those sessions' work had already merged (#10602, #10604) and `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` was CLEAN.

items.summary: Whether the half-built local LLM carries any weight is UNDECIDED — and it is undecided BY THE OPERATOR, not for want of evidence. ⚠️ THIS SUMMARY PREVIOUSLY ENDED '#10605 makes that arm dispatchable via LLMBENCH_MODEL_URL; it has NOT been run' — that was true when written and became FALSE on 2026-09-01, in the dangerous direction: a session reading only the summary would conclude the measurement is still owed and re-run a 16-minute job on the 1-core trainer under the heavy lock. BOTH SIZE ARMS ARE NOW MEASURED ON ANSWER QUALITY. 1.5B: fabricated a causal claim and misattributed the fault. 3B (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M, `RESULT: benchmarked`, `single-shot flag: -st`, both controls passing): better on BOTH of those specific defects — it hedges instead of inventing, and keeps the fault on the internal side — but never names the mechanism, at ~2.1x the latency and ~0.96 GB of headroom. So the REMAINING step is the operator's decision, which is the last clause of clears_when ('Then the operator decides'). Read the observation for the full sample and for one correction it carries: the truncation both models show is OURS (`-n 200`), not evidence about either model.
items.clears_when: A `llm_capacity_benchmark.sh` run under LLMBENCH_MODEL_URL reaches `RESULT: benchmarked` with `model:` naming the requested URL and NO `requested override did NOT serve` warning, and its generation sample is compared against the 1.5B baseline below on ANSWER QUALITY against the same real repo question. Then the operator decides. A throughput comparison alone does NOT clear this.
items.observation:
MEASURED 2026-08-31 on the trainer VM, post-reboot, RESULT: benchmarked, flag probe selected `--single-turn`. Throughput pp128 22.35 +/- 0.24, tg64 7.19 +/- 0.34 t/s (pre-reboot 22.53 / 7.38 — identical within noise). 36.4s wall, 2.86 GB peak RSS on a 5.9 GB box. THE QUALITY IS THE FINDING, NOT THE SPEED: the sample restated the prompt, FABRICATED a causal claim ('margin was calculated from the per-coin block, indicating that the available balance is less than the required margin' — two unrelated facts joined by an invented 'indicating'), MISATTRIBUTED the fault to venue liquidity when the defect was our own sizer reading an empty account-level field, and TRUNCATED mid-sentence without answering the third of the prompt asking what to check next. A model that confidently invents a cause is worse than no model on a system whose canonical rule is always-verify. THE SIZE EXPECTATION IS ARITHMETIC, NOT A MEASUREMENT — a 3B roughly halves the speed and should raise quality, a 0.5B does the reverse; do not quote either as a result. || 2026-08-31, session ayloee — THE DIFFERENT-SIZE ARM WAS RUN AND THIS ROW DOES NOT CLEAR, BY ITS OWN CRITERION. clears_when says in as many words that a throughput comparison alone does NOT clear it, and a throughput comparison is exactly what came back. Dispatched via LLMBENCH_MODEL_URL (issue #10621) with a dispatch-time positive control; `model:` named the requested Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M URL with NO fallback warning, so the arm is genuine. MEASURED: pp128 10.57 +/- 0.04, tg64 3.91 +/- 0.00 t/s, peak RSS 4,792,340 KB = 4.79 GB on the 5.9 GB box — 2.1x and 1.84x slower than the 1.5B, fitting with ~1.1 GB headroom. NOT MEASURED: the answer. RESULT was `benchmarked_throughput_only`, exit status 124 (timeout), 15:01.52 wall clock, and the captured output is fourteen `>` prompts then `Exiting...` — llama-cli sat in interactive mode and never generated. So nothing whatever may be concluded about 3B answer quality: not 'similar to the 1.5B', not 'presumably worse'. CAUSE, root-caused after two of my own explanations were refuted by measurement (the flag candidate list is NOT stale — `-st` and `--single-turn` are both in build e4b9af0's 562-line help; `--help` does NOT exit non-zero — it exits 0): SIGPIPE. `grep -q` exits on first match, closing the pipe while llama-cli is still writing; llama-cli dies 141 and the script's own `set -uo pipefail` makes the pipeline report 141, so the `if` was FALSE though grep had MATCHED. Measured all three arms (no-pipefail rc=0 / pipefail SKIPPED rc=141 / control TAKEN). Fixed by capturing --help once and matching with `case`. ⚠️ THIS IS THE THREE-STATE CONTRACT WORKING, NOT FAILING: #10597 exists so `benchmarked` is never printed over a generation step that did not run, and it was not — the run graded itself and named which half is valid. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-31: RE-RUN for the answer. It is queued against main once the SIGPIPE fix lands (PR #10620) and costs a full llama.cpp rebuild plus a 2 GB re-download on the 1-core trainer under the heavy lock — the EXIT trap cleaned up, disk back to 7.4 G. || 2026-09-01 (session 01HYXKHpDQeWv3u4rjWWoL2J): THE RE-RUN COMPLETED AND THE ANSWER IS NOW MEASURED — the row is READY FOR THE OPERATOR'S DECISION and is NOT cleared by me, because clears_when ends 'Then the operator decides.' Collected via trainer-diag #10642 off the run launched 2026-08-31T22:11:17Z, finished 22:27:49Z. BOTH CONTROLS PASS, which is what makes the sample gradeable at all: `single-shot flag: -st` (the SIGPIPE fix in #10620 works — the previous run's `benchmarked_throughput_only` is gone) and `RESULT: benchmarked`. DONE marker present, no process running, lock released, EXIT trap cleaned up (disk 7.4G). Throughput on the real generation path: pp128 9.67 +/- 1.27, tg64 3.91 +/- 0.00 t/s; end-to-end 10.5 t/s prompt / 3.7 t/s generation; 200 tokens in 71.07s wall at 96% CPU; peak RSS 4,947,364 KB = 4.95 GB on the 5.9 GB box, ~0.96 GB headroom. Consistent with the earlier throughput-only arm (10.57 / 3.91), so the speed answer has not moved: ~2.1x and ~1.84x slower than the 1.5B.

THE ANSWER, WHICH IS THE DELIVERABLE. Same prompt as the 1.5B baseline. THE 3B IS BETTER ON BOTH SPECIFIC DEFECTS THE 1.5B WAS FAILED FOR, and that is a real improvement rather than a hedge: (1) NO FABRICATED CAUSAL CLAIM — where the 1.5B joined two unrelated facts with an invented 'indicating', the 3B hedges correctly ('This suggests a discrepancy', 'could indicate issues with the margin calculation process'); (2) NO MISATTRIBUTION — the 1.5B blamed venue liquidity, while the 3B keeps the fault on the internal side ('the margin calculation process', 'the margin management system'), which is where the defect actually was. ⚠️ BUT IT NEVER NAMES THE MECHANISM. The real cause is that the sizer fell back to TOTAL EQUITY and counted initial margin already pledged to open positions as free (BL-20260813-ICTSCALP-BTC-BYBIT2-BALANCE-REJECTS, fixed by the coin_derived rung). The 3B produces generic-competent prose that restates the prompt and gestures at 'a discrepancy' — nothing a session could act on. ⚠️ AND CORRECT ONE THING IN THE BASELINE ABOVE: it attributes the 1.5B's truncation to the model ('TRUNCATED mid-sentence without answering the third of the prompt asking what to check next'). THE 3B TRUNCATES AT THE SAME PLACE — 3 complete bullets then a severed '- **Next Steps to' — and the cause is OURS, not the model's: the harness passes `-n 200`, a generation cap both runs hit. Truncation is therefore NOT evidence about either model and must not be counted against the 3B or re-quoted against the 1.5B; raising `-n` is the fix if the 'what to check next' third is ever to be graded.

SO THE MEASURED VERDICT IS: better where it was failed, still not useful, at ~2x the cost and ~1 GB of headroom on a 1-core box. My reading is that this does not carry weight for analysis work on a system whose canonical rule is always-verify — plausible generic prose is the failure mode that rule exists to catch — but the decision is the operator's and the row stays open for it.

items.observation: 2026-08-31, session ayloee — SHIPPED, NOT PROVEN. Local: 16 planted controls fire, verified under both a stripped environment and one carrying tokens (an ambient-env dependence in this very self-test was caught by CI earlier the same session, which is part of why the reader is not being taken on trust). Against the real API: zero runs. Nothing observed. || 2026-09-01 (session 01HYXKHpDQeWv3u4rjWWoL2J): THE READER HAS NOW RUN FOR REAL AND IT DOES NOT WORK — this row does NOT clear, and its own declared failure signal has fired. probes.yml run #32, workflow_dispatch on main, GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest, committed PROBES.json generated_at 2026-09-01T05:38:50Z. Both probe_actions_log rows: could_not_run / exit_2, '20 run(s) listed but NONE had readable logs (20 unread)' on gpu-burst-train.yml AND the same on guards.yml — 0 of 40. LISTING works, so the API is reachable and the bearer authenticates; LOG DOWNLOAD is what fails. ⚠️ TWO EXPLANATIONS ARE REFUTED, and recording that is worth more than the fix, because both were the standing hypotheses. (1) The handoff note said 'SUSPECT THE READER — api.github.com is 403 from a web sandbox'. That 403 is real and is NOT the cause here: this ran on a RUNNER, and the listing calls succeeded from the same process with the same token. A session chasing sandbox egress would find nothing. items.summary: replay-pregate-nightly's nightly red is NOT a network fault and NOT an OOM kill -- the trainer VM is out of memory and swap-thrashing, and the fleet run cannot finish. Both OOM greps -- `dmesg -T` and `journalctl --since -2h` -- returned EMPTY, so nothing was killed; the driver is alive and crawling. It scored 10 of 22 heads in 30 minutes and was still going.
items.detail: WHY THIS COULD NOT BE SEEN BEFORE, and why the repair was worth doing even though it does not fix the cause. Every previous run died at ~8m55s with `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe` at head 10/22 -- 7 of the 8 most recent scheduled runs, with two read in full (#4330, #4335->#4365) and IDENTICAL. A thrashing box stops answering its sshd, so the single long-lived interactive channel dropped and the job reported `no JSON object in driver output`: a parse error standing in for a memory problem, which is why five sessions in a row could act on none of it. With the run DETACHED the transport stopped being the confound: #4390's poll survived its entire 30-minute budget with ZERO transport failures, salvaged 10 heads, and the failure-path evidence step returned the numbers above. [!] SO THE TRANSPORT REPAIR IS PROVEN AND THE WORKFLOW IS STILL RED, and those are different facts. [!] THE OOM HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, NOT UNCONFIRMED -- the shipping session deliberately declined to assert it, and the kernel evidence says it would have been wrong. [!] A THIRD DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE SAME RUN AND IS PRE-EXISTING: the commit-back step ran `git add "$DIR"` on runtime_logs/replay_pregate, which .gitignore:29 refuses outright, so under `set -e` it destroyed the 10 salvaged heads. `git ls-tree -r origin/main -- runtime_logs/replay_pregate/` returns ZERO files across the repo's whole fetched history while 72 other runtime_logs files ARE tracked -- so this workflow's own header claim, that it 'commits the report back to the repo, so the result survives a dead Claude session', has been false since it was written, on the COMPLETE path as much as the partial one. Fixed with `git add -f`.
